successors.note: North of the Taedong the Tang kept Liaodong; the protectorate itself survived with its seat moved to Liaodong (676), Xincheng/Fushun (677), Pingzhou (714), Liaoxi (743) and was 'abandoned in 756 or ended in 761' (Protectorate page); this dossier covers only the Korean phase.

capitals.name: Old City of Liaodong (Liaoyang)
capitals.note: 'In the second month of the third year of the Shangyuan era [676], the seat of Andong was moved to the Old City of Liaodong' (footnote); the Protectorate page has 'forced to relocate ... to Liaoyang' in 676 and Xincheng (Fushun) in 677.

correction.text: Goguryeo's territory in Manchuria and the northern Korean peninsula: 'divided into 9 commanderies, 42 prefectures, and 100 counties' (the 667 outline is the last full one)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Goguryeo shape, 360,601 km2, runs to 673 and a Tang shape contains the land). The Protectorate page gives 9 commanderies, 42 prefectures, 100 counties and an estimated '697,000 Goguryeo households' and no area. Goguryeo's own revolts (669-673) and Silla's pressure from 670 are wars, not changes of this outline until 676.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 676, Silla took all the territory south of the Taedong River' and the seat left Pyongyang in February. One year only; from 677 the Tang hold Liaodong and the Taedong is the border (Protectorate page: recognised by the Tang in 736).

region.text: Goguryeo's territory in Manchuria and the northern Korean peninsula: 'divided into 9 commanderies, 42 prefectures, and 100 counties' (the 667 outline is the last full one)

ledger.note: December 668: the Tang divide Goguryeo into the Protectorate. 'In the twelfth month of that year [668], Goguryeo's territory was divided into 9 commanderies, 42 prefectures, and 100 counties' (footnote); 'In the ninth month ... the Minister of Works Li Ji pacified Goguryeo'. The Protectorate page: created at Pyongyang after the conquest.

February 676: the seat leaves Pyongyang. 'In the second month of the third year of the Shangyuan era [676], the seat of Andong was moved to the Old City of Liaodong'; Graff's note: the Tang 'withdraw the headquarters of its Korean protectorate to the Liao River valley in the early months of 676'.

region.text: 'Silla took all the territory south of the Taedong River' (676): Hwanghae and Gyeonggi are the Goguryeo-held lands south of it

ledger.note: 676: Silla takes the land south of the Taedong. 'In 676, Silla took all the territory south of the Taedong River in a series of battles'; the war 'ended with a Silla victory at Gibeolpo in November'. The Tang formally recognised the line in 736.

region.text: Goguryeo's territory in Manchuria and the northern Korean peninsula: 'divided into 9 commanderies, 42 prefectures, and 100 counties' (the 667 outline is the last full one)

ledger.note: 676: the Korean protectorate ends. Seat moved to Liaodong, then Xincheng (677); the protectorate itself lasts to 756/761 elsewhere. The Cliopatria Goguryeo sliver of 674-681 (148 km2) is not explained by any page.

wars.name: Goguryeo revolts against the Protectorate
wars.outcome: 'the first revolt of the people of Goguryeo took place in 669' and from 670 to 673 'the rebels launched an uprising every year, the last of which lasted for four years'; the Tang held the northern lands.
wars.note: Silla supported the loyalists; no border moved until 676.

wars.name: Silla-Tang War

zones.text: 'Silla took all the territory south of the Taedong River' (676): Hwanghae and Gyeonggi are the Goguryeo-held lands south of it

wars.note: The lead says 668-676, the infobox 670-676; the Tang example uses 670.

certainty.note: Goguryeo outline; occupation lines moved with the revolts.
The Taedong River line, the frontier Silla won and the Tang recognised in 736.

sources.title: Protectorate General to Pacify the East
sources.note: Created at Pyongyang after 668; 9 commanderies, 42 prefectures; seats 676 Liaoyang, 677 Xincheng, 714, 743; ended 756/761.

sources.title: Silla-Tang War
sources.note: Dates: 668 division of Goguryeo (footnote), 669-673 revolts, 675 Maeso, 676 Taedong line and Gibeolpo, 676 seat move.

notes: Colony (Tang protectorate) for the Korean phase 668-676 only, so the protectorate's later life (Liaodong 676/677, Xincheng, Pingzhou 714, Liaoxi 743, end 756/761) is inside the tang-dynasty dossier's land. The tang-dynasty example already carries a 668 gain of Goguryeo and a 676 loss; this dossier lets the renderer draw the occupation as a Tang colony tint rather than as direct Tang land. Not covered: the Ungjin Commandery in Baekje's former land (660-671, jk-02-b flagged it; no page opened here dates it), Gyerim (refused) and Gao Zang / Gao Jiansheng (not on the Protectorate page; its commander list gives Wei Zhe 668-669, Xue Rengui 669-670, Gao Kan 670-676, Bojang 677-681, Qu Tuquan 681-685, Xue Ne 685-696). The page text disagrees with itself on the 676 seat (Liaoyang against 'the Old City of Liaodong') and on the end of the protectorate (756 or 761). Goguryeo's Cliopatria row runs to 681 with a 148 km2 sliver (jk-02-b: wrong).
